newsitem.title: USA: Hot, dry weather stresses Missouri corn/soy crops.
newsitem.headline: Hot, dry weather stresses Missouri corn/soy crops.

text.p: Corn and soybean conditions declined in the week ended Sunday as more hot, dry weather stressed the crops, according to the Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service.
"Late weekend rain across some northern counties was of considerable benefit but most areas will need rain soon to maintain yield potential," the report said.

Topsoil moisture was rated 20 percent very short, 50 percent short, 29 percent adequate and one percent surplus. Subsoil moisture was rated 10 percent very short, 44 percent short, 45 percent adequate and one percent surplus.
Corn was silking on 83 percent of the acreage, about 10 days ahead of average. The crop was rated two percent very poor, 12 percent poor, 40 percent fair, 41 percent good and five percent excellent.

Soybeans were blooming on 62 percent of the acreage, about one day ahead of the five-year average. The crop was rated three percent very poor, 13 percent poor, 41 percent fair, 39 percent good and four percent excellent.
Pasture was rated five percent very poor, 25 percent poor, 44 percent fair, 25 percent good and one percent excellent.
